results.finding: sections, unit counts and unit forms match the spec

All 43 aligned units summarise the controlling idea of their spec paragraph in spec order (p01-p43, how-written in locus order: stance, five kinds, confusions, materials, no internal material, dates, as-of). The four callouts are unaligned by design.

Three units flagged two_ideas: the KEY POINTS callout (three bullets by design), Introduction ¶4 (aim + roadmap, both in spec p04's controlling idea and transition), Veldmark and the Toolkit ¶2 (toolkit + glossary, both in spec p39's controlling idea). None is a stray second idea.

Every unit traces to I1-I5: scene and failure patterns to I1, the argument to I2, who/why-exists to I3, how-written, Veldmark and living journal to I4, organization/decision/toolkit and conclusion to I5.

Scenario evidence (scene, green reports, four leaks) is interpreted in Introduction ¶2-¶3; Figure 1 and Figure 2 sit under paragraphs that state what they show; the five-kinds table is followed by the three confusions; the overview table and Figure 4 are unpacked part by part; the routing table is explained in two paragraphs; the Adevinta quotations are explained ('Both statements were true when they were written'); the Veldmark scenario and pattern names are framed as previews of the next pages.

Every declared transition_in is expressed at its boundary (e.g. contrast 'Every team in the room has a good answer for its own part', cause_effect 'Judging a marketplace as one machine needs material that connects its stages', sequence 'Those are the rules for weighing what the book says; next is how it is laid out', contrast 'Part IX, PRACTICE, steps outside the fiction', conclusion_summary 'That is the argument, the routes into the book and the rules for weighing it'). Part V's sequence step relies on the part numbering only, which suffices.

Organising principle: both readers describe the page as ordered by the questions a newcomer needs answered, from 'is this for me' to 'where next', following the roadmap exactly, with the map before the routing shortcut. This agrees with the declared prerequisite_order plus large_to_small; no section's position was unclear. Material lost-thread points are reported separately.

results.quote: Whatever its kind, every statement in the book, except a Veldmark illustration, rests on three kinds of material, and no other.
results.finding: flowA item b: re-read because a second 'kinds' classification starts right after the five-kinds table, and 'every statement ... rests on ... and no other' seems to contradict the table's 'No source validates it' for recommendations. The spec order is fine; the wording reuses 'kinds' and overclaims.

results.quote: The book started from two generic domain models of marketplace businesses from Productscape, my sibling repository of business domain models
results.finding: flowA item c: the domain-models bullet 'came out of nowhere'; an origin story about an unexplained sibling repository, listed first, inside sourcing rules. Fix is in the prose (frame it as a plain source, or put it last).

results.quote: Of the three kinds of material, the public record of the named companies ages fastest.
results.finding: flowA item d: attention drifted in the long how-written section; the dated Adevinta example felt like a return to the date rule already given in the table. The rationale sits two blocks away from the rule it explains. This comes from the spec's paragraph order (materials and no-internal-material before dates), which also contradicts the section's own flow rationale ('The material every statement rests on comes last').

results.quote: Whichever route you take, a chapter of Parts I to VIII opens with two things this page has not yet introduced, and each has its own preface page next
results.finding: flowA item f: re-read because 'this page has not yet introduced' is untrue; How the Book Is Organized ¶11 already named 'a Veldmark scene that poses the question', and Veldmark appears several times earlier. flowB also found 'each has its own preface page next' hard to parse. The spec's order is fine; the bridge sentence is wrong.

results.quote: Veldmark is where the book rehearses decisions; the **[[toolkit]]** is what you use to make your own.
results.finding: flowA item i: grouping the toolkit and glossary (reference material already in the organization table's Reference row) with the fictional company felt forced, and the glossary sentence an add-on. The pairing is fixed by the spec's section design.
results.corroborated_by: flowB section (2), Veldmark and the Toolkit: 'the pairing is a little loose'

results.quote: It maps each part to the stage of the machine that part designs, the guarantee that stage must give, the liquidity metric the stage protects and the failure pattern that appears when the guarantee fails.
results.finding: flowA item a only: a jump ahead in the middle of the thesis, using parts and failure patterns before the page introduces them. The spec's controlling idea needs only 'draws the argument together into fitness functions'; the prose adds the forward-referencing detail.

results.quote: Facts in this book were checked against public sources in October 2026 unless a chapter says otherwise.
results.finding: flowA item e only: how current the book is gets split between How This Book Is Written and A Living Journal, which the roadmap names as the place for 'how the book is kept current'. That split comes from where the spec places the as-of paragraph.

Terms the reader does not know are given or explicitly deferred: matches and liquidity are defined before use (local, compounds); mandates, feed imports, alert e-mails, moderation queue, recommerce and fitness functions are glossed at first use; DSA and VINs are expanded; learning to rank and percolation are named only as terms 'defined where they first matter, in the chapter that owns them'. Engineering terms (event streams, aggregate, bounded contexts) are within already_knows. Opaque pattern names (Multiplier Creep, Deal-Shaped Architecture) are framed as names the next page unpacks; both flow readers called them minor.
Opens on a puzzling scenario (the general manager's chart), not a dictionary definition, a broad generalisation or an announcement; the roadmap follows the hook.
No mere restatement or new topic: the conclusion routes readers and turns the opening question into a design lens.

Where to Go Next ¶2 synthesises parts, routing table, patterns and Veldmark into one question ('which liquidity does it protect or spend, and at which boundary?') and gives the so-what: the question 'can be traced to a hand-off and an owner'.
'keep the general manager's question in mind: why does a smaller competitor turn its listings into more contacts?' and 'which no team's green report answers' call back to the opening scene.

The intro reader listed the seven sections in roadmap order (who; argument and why; labels and sources; parts and routing table; failure patterns; Veldmark and toolkit; how kept current), the hand-off to the next two preface pages, and evidence: an openly invented business-review scene plus dated documented facts. This matches the expected answer.

Reader stated the liquidity-machine argument (turning fresh, trustworthy supply into matches with demand; local and compounding) and listed Parts I-IX in order: marketplace, listing, supply, discovery, trust, money, platform, leadership agenda, public cases. Matches expected.
